## Full annotations

<a id="flexa-mem"></a>

## FlexA-Mem: Budget-Adaptive Agentic Memory for LLM Agents

**2026-10-23 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33274)

**Mechanism.** Keeps an immutable history store and constructs a query-specific context from a timeline plus retrieved detail under a fixed token budget. Its fixed rendering rules provide a useful baseline for learned memory systems.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** both. **Learning signal:** New history records and current queries; rendering follows a fixed rule.

**Evaluation.** The abstract reports AppWorld task-completion experiments and LongMemEval and LoCoMo QA, including an unused-task evaluation with predictions fixed beforehand.

**Boundary.** The method adapts the presented context rather than learning its own update policy. It is included as an adjacent comparison for separating memory access gains from agent self-learning.

**Code / data.** Code availability not verified in this review.

**Topics:** memory, evaluation. **Reviewed:** abstract · 2026-10-28.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33274)

<a id="trusting-trust-agents"></a>

## Reflections on Trusting Trust, Revisited: Contaminating Self-Modifying AI Coding Agents with Poisoned Benchmarks

**2026-09-15 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17817)

**Mechanism.** Studies whether poisoned optimization benchmarks can induce persistent changes that cause self-modifying coding agents to emit vulnerable code on later clean tasks.

**What changes:** Agent code, Prompts / context, Tools. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Benchmark feedback during the self-modification process.

**Evaluation.** Presents proof-of-concept studies on a modified Darwin Gödel Machine, SICA, and Hyperagents, including continued evolution after poison removal.

**Boundary.** These are constructed attacks under specified agent and benchmark conditions, not an estimate of attack prevalence. Clean subsequent tasks do not reliably remove contaminated components in the studied cases.

**Code / data.** No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.

**Topics:** safety, evaluation, recursive-improvement. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-28.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17817) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.17817v1)

<a id="modularrsi"></a>

## ModularRSI: Modular and Generalizable Recursive Harness Self-Improvement

**2026-09-14 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14857)

**Mechanism.** Evolves five harness modules in separate restricted lineages, then integrates their changes. The evolved agent performs trajectory analysis and code modification; a function library controls reuse and redundancy.

**What changes:** Agent code, Tools, Workflows, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Contrasts between successful and failed trajectories, followed by validation gates.

**Evaluation.** Evolution uses a separately constructed task collection; the frozen learned library is evaluated on TerminalBench 2.0 and SWE-bench Verified, including cross-model transfer.

**Boundary.** The reported benchmark separation depends on the documented curation and similarity-screening procedure. Infrastructure is outside the editable scope, and downstream evaluation allows function selection but no further function modification.

**Code / data.** Official code availability was not established in this source review.

**Topics:** architecture, recursive-improvement, evaluation, tools. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-28.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14857) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.14857v2)

<a id="safety-self-evolving-survey"></a>

## Safety in Self-Evolving Agents: A Survey

**2026-09-08 · preprint · core · survey**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00093)

**Mechanism.** Uses a transition-centered framework to examine how reusable state acquires influence, changes scope, and propagates failures through later adaptations.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.

**Evaluation.** Reviews evidence for admission, retrieval, activation, containment, and repair; identifies comparatively weak evidence for repairing descendants and evaluating resumed learning.

**Boundary.** The framework proposes how to organize longitudinal safety assessment; it does not certify that a learning system remains safe.

**Code / data.** No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.

**Topics:** surveys, safety, evaluation, memory. **Reviewed:** abstract · 2026-10-28.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00093)

<a id="phantom-gains"></a>

## Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null

**2026-08-20 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20290)

**Mechanism.** Runs frozen-model controls through the same pipeline as self-training to estimate how decoding and measurement noise can create apparent per-problem capability changes.

**What changes:** Analysis / no retained update. **Persistence:** not-applicable. **Learning signal:** Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.

**Evaluation.** Audits repeated low-rank self-training and matched alternatives, proposing per-problem tests against pooled baseline replicates.

**Boundary.** The reported measurement failures are valuable controls for study design; results from one training setup do not establish that every self-training method fails.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/chengxuphd/phantom-gains) — Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.

<a id="hyperskill"></a>

## HyperSkill: Self-Evolving LLM Agents via Hypergraph-Structured Skill Memory

**2026-08-17 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16114)

**Mechanism.** Connects reusable skills and subtask steps through trajectory-level hyperedges. Retrieval combines subtask and trajectory evidence, while periodic maintenance merges redundant skills and prunes low-utility entries.

**What changes:** Skills, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Trajectory relationships and quality or utility signals used during memory maintenance.

**Evaluation.** The authors compare memory baselines on xBench, GAIA, and WebWalkerQA with two language-model backbones.

**Boundary.** This annotation is based on the primary abstract. Interpretation: benchmark comparisons do not independently establish long-term retention or safe pruning under changing task distributions.

**Code / data.** Code availability not verified in this review.

**Topics:** skills, memory. **Reviewed:** abstract · 2026-10-28.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16114)

<a id="hierarchical-self-improvement"></a>

## Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Harnesses

**2026-08-09 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08466)

**Mechanism.** Uses a frozen model at three levels: task execution, harness editing, and editing the strategy used by the harness evolver. Each task family maintains a reusable evolving harness.

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Environment rewards evaluated under a fixed outer anchor.

**Evaluation.** BALROG experiments report gains on several game environments, held-out BabaIsAI sub-suites, and no improvement on NLE.

**Boundary.** The authors identify limits from feedback quality and the frozen model capability. The outer anchor remains fixed, and held-out results concern the particular task-family splits.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/TailinZhou/hsi) — Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.

**Topics:** architecture, recursive-improvement, evaluation. **Reviewed:** abstract · 2026-10-28.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08466) · [Source 2](https://github.com/TailinZhou/hsi)

<a id="evolvenet"></a>

## EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement

**2026-08-05 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04968)

**Mechanism.** Different clients evolve copies of a shared harness on local tasks. A server combines compatible program adaptations and redistributes the result so later evolution can reuse discoveries from other clients.

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Local workload feedback and evidence-guided validation of combined program changes.

**Evaluation.** The revised abstract reports five experimental settings and ablations separating adaptation composition from selecting a single specialist.

**Boundary.** The theoretical results are conditional on assumptions about retaining and composing improvements. Curator interpretation: sharing code adaptations without raw workloads does not by itself establish a formal privacy guarantee.

**Code / data.** Official code availability was not established in this source review.

**Topics:** architecture, workflows, continual-learning. **Reviewed:** abstract · 2026-10-28.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04968)

<a id="past-bench"></a>

## PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents

**2026-08-04 · preprint · core · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04003)

**Mechanism.** Uses ordered fresh-session tasks with matched retention-on and retention-off conditions, and records evidence for saving, retrieving, and updating persistent state.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Earlier task experience and explicit state updates; controls remove or corrupt retained information.

**Evaluation.** Tests personal-agent frameworks across memory, procedural reuse, information gathering, and update, with diagnostic interventions in Hermes+.

**Boundary.** The controlled families and model-dependent gains test prerequisites for recursive improvement, not an open-ended recursive process. Task scores and intended mechanism evidence are separate outcomes.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/Gen-Verse/PAST-Bench) — Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.

**Topics:** evaluation, memory, skills, continual-learning, recursive-improvement. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-28.

[Source 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04003) · [Source 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.04003v1) · [Source 3](https://github.com/Gen-Verse/PAST-Bench)

<a id="gdpevo"></a>

## GDPevo: Evaluating Agent Self-Evolution on Real Business Tasks

**2026-08-04 · preprint · core · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03764)

**Mechanism.** Distributes hidden business rules across training tasks and recombines them in held-out tasks, using an automated pipeline to construct environments and deterministic graders.

**What changes:** Skills, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Training tasks with controlled supervision; held-out rules are recombinations of training evidence.

**Evaluation.** Compares agent/model combinations and supervision types on generated enterprise workflow tasks and analyzes rule transfer.

**Boundary.** Construction calibrates task groups partly for an expected improvement range, which can favor detectable learning gains. These are generated business scenarios, not a live enterprise deployment study.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/Prism-Shadow/GDPevo) — Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.

**Topics:** evaluation, skills, applications, continual-learning. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-28.

<a id="agentstream"></a>

## AgentStream: How Well Do Self-Evolving LLM Agents Perform Under Streaming Tasks?

**2026-07-31 · preprint · core · benchmark**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00155)

**Mechanism.** Evaluates retained agent state under isolated domain streams, sequential domain shifts, and interleaved tasks, comparing each evolving agent with a no-evolution baseline.

**What changes:** Memory, Skills, Prompts / context, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Execution outcomes and model-generated feedback; ground-truth test labels are withheld from adaptation.

**Evaluation.** Crosses five methods with three model backbones and six benchmarks; method benefits vary with the model and stream composition.

**Boundary.** The paper limits model-strength conclusions to its framework and selected benchmarks. Streaming performance is not proof of indefinite retention or deployment reliability.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/Jasper-Yan/AgentStream) — Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.

**Topics:** evaluation, continual-learning, memory, skills, workflows. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-28.

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.17308)

**Mechanism.** Starts agents without skills and carries a library of trajectory- and rubric-derived skill patches through sequential tasks within task families.

<a id="hyperagents"></a>

## Hyperagents

**2026-03-19 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19461)

**Mechanism.** Combines the task solver and the agent that modifies it in one editable program. DGM-Hyperagents can therefore revise their own improvement procedure as well as task-solving code.

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows, Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task evaluation and archived improvement histories, including transfer tests for the meta-agent.

**Evaluation.** The study includes coding, paper-review prediction, robotics reward design, and math-solution grading, with held-out task evaluations and cross-domain tests of the meta-agent.

**Boundary.** The main experiments retain a fixed task distribution and outer selection/evaluation protocol. The paper establishes bounded transfer of improvement procedures, not unconstrained or indefinitely accelerating self-improvement.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Hyperagents) — Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.

**Topics:** recursive-improvement, architecture, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-28.

<a id="skillrl"></a>

## SkillRL: Evolving Agents via Recursive Skill-Augmented Reinforcement Learning

**2026-02-09 · preprint · NeurIPS 2026 acceptance reported by authors; venue record not inspected · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08234)

**Mechanism.** Distills successful and failed trajectories into a hierarchical skill library, retrieves those skills during policy training, and adds lessons from validation failures. The library and model policy change together during reinforcement learning.

**What changes:** Skills, Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task rewards, teacher-generated skill distillation, and validation failures.

**Evaluation.** The authors evaluate ALFWorld, WebShop, and seven search-augmented QA datasets, including component and teacher-model analyses.

**Boundary.** The method uses a teacher and reward-bearing environments, so it is not training-free or supervision-free. Interpretation: its recursive skill refresh is not evidence that the system can redesign its own learning algorithm.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/aiming-lab/SkillRL) — Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.

**Topics:** skills, memory, model-training. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-28.

## Group-Evolving Agents: Open-Ended Self-Improvement via Experience Sharing

**2026-02-04 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04837)

**Mechanism.** Treats a group of agents as the unit of evolution, allowing discoveries from different branches to influence later designs. It aims to reuse exploratory diversity that would otherwise remain isolated in individual lineages.

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Shared experience across a group of agent variants and coding-task evaluations.

**Evaluation.** Evaluations use SWE-bench Verified and Polyglot, with model-transfer and framework-bug recovery analyses.

**Boundary.** The evidence concerns coding agents under the study budgets. Curator interpretation: experience sharing during search is distinct from a deployed multi-agent team continually learning in an open environment.

**Code / data.** Official code availability was not established in this source review.

## Dr. Zero: Self-Evolving Search Agents without Training Data

**2026-01-11 · peer-reviewed · COLM 2026 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.07055)

**Mechanism.** Co-evolves a proposer that generates diverse, challenging questions and a search-enabled solver. Hop-grouped policy optimization shares baselines among structurally similar questions to reduce training overhead.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Proposer–solver feedback grounded in an external search environment.

**Evaluation.** The authors compare the trained search agents with supervised alternatives on several question-answering benchmarks.

**Boundary.** Without training data means without human-annotated task data, not without external information: the search engine supplies a knowledge environment. This abstract-level review does not independently test search freshness, citation fidelity, or long-term robustness.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.

**Topics:** model-training, self-play, tools, applications. **Reviewed:** abstract · 2026-10-28.

**2026-01-08 · preprint · core · paper**

**Mechanism.** Externalizes improvement into a release pipeline that constructs one candidate at a time. Promotion emphasizes which previously passing tasks fail and which failing tasks are repaired.

**What changes:** Agent code, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Implementation-blind trace critiques, executable diagnosis, and per-task regression/fix outcomes.

**Evaluation.** The abstract reports execution-heavy benchmark experiments with fewer regressions and auditable version histories.

**Boundary.** This is an external improvement pipeline rather than in-agent autonomous learning. The abstract review does not establish the benchmark composition, statistical uncertainty, or protection against every regression.

**2026-01-06 · preprint · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03192)

**Mechanism.** Uses outcome feedback to adjust the utility of episodic memories while keeping the reasoning model fixed. Two-stage retrieval combines semantic relevance with learned utility to select useful past strategies.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Environment feedback updates the utility assigned to episodic memories.

**Evaluation.** The authors report results on HLE, BigCodeBench, ALFWorld, and Lifelong Agent Bench.

**Boundary.** The abstract and official repository were inspected; training/evaluation separation and statistical uncertainty were not independently audited. Benchmark gains do not settle the stability-plasticity problem in general.

**Mechanism.** Equips a coding agent with tools to edit its own implementation and reuses improved versions in later iterations. Learning changes the surrounding agent code rather than model parameters.

**What changes:** Agent code, Tools, Workflows. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Benchmark feedback and LLM reflection on candidate code changes.

**Evaluation.** The paper reports gains on a random SWE-bench Verified subset, LiveCodeBench, and synthetic agent tasks.

**Boundary.** The software-repair result uses a fixed 50-task subset and a five-minute timeout. The authors note that faster file editing explains part of the gain, with limited improvements on reasoning tasks; repeated benchmark evaluation is distinct from held-out deployment transfer.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/MaximeRobeyns/self_improving_coding_agent) — Official repository linked in the paper and landing page inspected; not executed.

**Topics:** architecture, recursive-improvement, applications. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-28.

**2024-09-19 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2025 · core · paper**

**Mechanism.** Trains a correction policy on its own response distribution, with an initialization stage and a reward bonus encouraging successful revision. The method targets distribution mismatch and collapsed correction behavior observed in offline supervised training.

## AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data

**2024-07-24 · peer-reviewed · Nature 2024 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07566-y)

**Mechanism.** Analyzes how repeated training on generated data can lose low-probability parts of an original distribution and amplify errors. The paper combines tractable distribution models with generative-model experiments.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Recursive resampling and training on prior-generation model outputs.

**Evaluation.** Experiments include Gaussian mixtures, variational autoencoders, and repeated language-model fine-tuning, with differing amounts of original data retained.

**Boundary.** The theoretical replacement setting and finite experiments have specific data-mixing assumptions. Curator interpretation: this is a warning about recursive data use, not a proof that every verified or data-accumulating self-learning loop must fail.

**Code / data.** Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.

**Topics:** model-training, safety, evaluation. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-28.

**2024-04-01 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01413)

**Mechanism.** Compares replacement of earlier datasets with accumulation of original and synthetic data. It supplies a linear-model analysis and generative-model experiments showing that the data-retention policy changes collapse behavior.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Repeated generated-data training with old data retained rather than replaced.

**Evaluation.** The study includes small transformer language models on TinyStories, molecular diffusion, image variational autoencoders, and controlled analytical models.

**Boundary.** The bounded-error theorem is for its stated linear setting, and retaining growing datasets changes resource requirements. Curator interpretation: these results challenge universal collapse claims without certifying arbitrary self-training or agent-memory loops.

## Promptbreeder: Self-Referential Self-Improvement via Prompt Evolution

**2023-09-28 · peer-reviewed · ICML 2024 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16797)

**Mechanism.** Evolves a population of task instructions together with the instructions that produce their mutations. It provides a concrete example of changing part of the improvement procedure as well as the task-solving prompt.

**What changes:** Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Fitness on task examples guides selection of task prompts and mutation prompts.

**Evaluation.** Evaluations cover arithmetic, commonsense reasoning, and hate-speech classification.

**Boundary.** The foundation model and surrounding evolutionary procedure remain fixed. Prompt-level self-reference should not be read as evidence of unbounded improvement of the complete agent.

## Large Language Models as Optimizers

**2023-09-07 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2024 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.03409)

**Mechanism.** Uses an LLM to propose candidates from a history of instructions and their measured scores. Selected instructions can be reused on new examples without changing model weights.

**What changes:** Prompts / context. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Scores of earlier candidate prompts on a development task.

**Evaluation.** Prompt optimization is evaluated on GSM8K and BIG-Bench Hard, alongside illustrative numerical and combinatorial optimization tasks.

**Boundary.** This is an external prompt-search procedure, not evidence of autonomous lifelong agent learning. Curator interpretation: the chosen objective and development data constrain what the search can improve.

## ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners

**2023-08-20 · peer-reviewed · AAAI 2024 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.10144)

**Mechanism.** Collects training-task trajectories, contrasts successes and failures to extract reusable textual insights, and retrieves relevant experiences for new tasks. Learning changes the external experience and insight stores without updating the base model.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task outcomes and model-generated comparisons of successful and unsuccessful trajectories.

**Evaluation.** The paper evaluates HotpotQA, ALFWorld, and WebShop, examines insight and retrieval ablations, and studies transfer from question answering to fact verification.

**Boundary.** The investigated environments have textual observations and are deterministic. The authors note that larger lifelong insight stores would need additional retrieval beyond fitting all insights into context.

<a id="rest"></a>

## Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) for Language Modeling

**2023-08-17 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08998)

**Mechanism.** Alternates generating a batch of candidate outputs and improving the policy with offline reinforcement learning. Reusing generated data reduces the need to sample a new online batch for every update.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** A reward-based training objective applied to batches sampled from the current policy.

**Evaluation.** The reported experiments focus on machine translation, assessed using automatic metrics and human evaluation.

**Boundary.** This is externally organized model training on a specific application. Curator interpretation: the study does not establish a lifelong agent or a reward signal that itself improves without outside specification.

## Large Language Models as Tool Makers

**2023-05-26 · peer-reviewed · ICLR 2024 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.17126)

**Mechanism.** Separates tool creation from tool use, allowing a stronger model to create reusable programs that a cheaper model can invoke on related requests. A functional cache retains these capabilities across requests.

**What changes:** Tools. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Task examples and feedback from producing and using generated tools.

**Evaluation.** The paper compares task accuracy and serving cost on reasoning problems, including BIG-Bench tasks.

**Boundary.** Results depend on the selected task families and how tool-making costs are amortized. Interpretation: reusable tool creation does not establish unrestricted autonomous software evolution.

## Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models

**2023-05-25 · peer-reviewed · TMLR 2024 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291)

**Mechanism.** Builds an expanding library of executable Minecraft skills, retrieved and composed for later tasks. An automatic curriculum proposes objectives, while execution feedback and a model-based critic guide program repair before a skill is retained.

**What changes:** Skills, Tools. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Environment observations, interpreter errors, and model-based task verification.

**Evaluation.** The authors compare exploration, technology-tree progress, ablations, and reuse of learned skills on new tasks in another Minecraft world.

## MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory

**2023-05-17 · peer-reviewed · AAAI 2024 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10250)

**Mechanism.** Maintains retrievable interaction memories and user summaries, with time- and importance-sensitive forgetting and reinforcement. The SiliconFriend application combines this memory mechanism with a separately tuned conversational model.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Past interactions, elapsed time, and assigned memory importance.

**Evaluation.** The paper combines qualitative user-dialogue analysis with quantitative tests on model-generated long-term conversations.

**Boundary.** Simulated dialogue and personalization outcomes are not clinical validation or evidence of general task-skill improvement. The memory mechanism should be distinguished from separate model tuning.

## Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior

**2023-04-07 · peer-reviewed · UIST 2023 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03442)

**Mechanism.** Stores experiences, synthesizes higher-level reflections, and retrieves relevant memories to plan behavior in a simulated town. The accumulated state shapes subsequent actions and social interactions.

**What changes:** Memory. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Observed simulated events and model-generated reflections.

**Evaluation.** The authors assess behavioral believability and emergent coordination in a sandbox populated by simulated agents, including architecture ablations.

**Boundary.** Believability is a different outcome from task competence or factual correctness. This is an adjacent foundation for persistent reflective memory, not a demonstration of open-ended capability improvement.

## Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools

**2023-02-09 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2023 · core · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761)

**Mechanism.** Teaches a language model when to call a predefined API, which arguments to produce, and how to incorporate the returned information. The learned capability is stored in model parameters rather than a growing tool library.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Self-supervised tool-use examples seeded by a small number of demonstrations for each API.

**Evaluation.** The paper evaluates zero-shot downstream tasks using tools such as a calculator, question answering, search, translation, and a calendar.

**Boundary.** The available APIs and initial demonstrations are supplied by researchers. Curator interpretation: learning to invoke these tools is distinct from autonomously creating new tools or learning continually after deployment.

## Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions

**2023 · peer-reviewed · ACL 2023 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://aclanthology.org/2023.acl-long.754/)

**Mechanism.** Bootstraps an instruction-tuning dataset from the model, filters unsuitable examples, and fine-tunes the original model on the retained data. It is a foundation for synthetic-data learning rather than a deployed agent that learns during use.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Model-generated instruction/input/output examples filtered for invalidity and similarity.

**Evaluation.** The paper evaluates instruction following on Super-NaturalInstructions and expert-written novel tasks, including human assessment.

**Boundary.** The generator inherits its pretrained capabilities and biases, and dataset filtering is part of the learning system. Curator interpretation: better instruction following alone is not evidence of continual agent learning.

**2022-12-15 · preprint · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08073)

**Mechanism.** Uses self-critiques and revisions for supervised learning, then learns a preference model from AI comparisons and optimizes the assistant with reinforcement learning. The process automates parts of supervision while retaining an externally chosen constitution.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Human-authored principles guide AI critiques, revisions, and preference judgments.

**Evaluation.** The authors report human evaluations of helpfulness and harmlessness for trained assistants.

**Boundary.** The constitution and training procedure are designed externally. Curator interpretation: this supports AI-assisted alignment training, not unsupervised value discovery or a guarantee that safety persists through later self-modification.

<a id="star"></a>

## STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning

**2022-03-28 · peer-reviewed · NeurIPS 2022 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.14465)

**Mechanism.** Generates reasoning traces, keeps traces ending in the reference answer, and fine-tunes on them. Failed problems can be retried with the answer supplied as a hint; each outer iteration retrains from the original base model on the newly collected traces.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Known correct answers filter generated rationales; answer hints support rationalization of failed examples.

**Evaluation.** Experiments cover arithmetic, CommonsenseQA, and GSM8K, with comparisons to direct-answer fine-tuning and prompted reasoning.

**Boundary.** The method needs training questions, reference answers, and a small rationale seed. Correct final answers do not independently certify that every intermediate explanation is valid.

**Code / data.** [Official artifact](https://github.com/ezelikman/STaR) — Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.

**Topics:** foundations, model-training. **Reviewed:** full-text · 2026-10-28.

## Mastering the game of Go without human knowledge

**2017-10-19 · peer-reviewed · Nature 2017 · adjacent · paper**

[Primary source](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature24270)

**Mechanism.** Trains a policy/value network on games generated by its own search, then uses the updated network to improve subsequent search and play. This is an early concrete example of a coupled data-generation and policy-improvement loop.

**What changes:** Model weights. **Persistence:** across-tasks. **Learning signal:** Game outcomes and search-improved move selections from self-play.

**Evaluation.** The authors evaluate playing strength against earlier Go programs, including the previously published champion-defeating AlphaGo.

**Boundary.** The environment supplies exact rules, legal moves, and a reliable win/loss signal. Curator interpretation: success in this closed game does not establish open-ended language-agent learning.
